user.title: Intex Pool — Tuya cloud
user.description: Enter your Tuya IoT developer-cloud credentials once. Your devices and their local keys are discovered automatically, and IPs are found on your network — no manual key or IP entry. (Tick “set up manually” if you'd rather enter everything by hand.)

data_description.region: The data center of your Tuya IoT project (eu, us, cn or in).
data_description.access_id: The Access ID/Client ID from your project's overview page on iot.tuya.com.
data_description.access_secret: The Access Secret/Client Secret from the same page.
data_description.manual: Skip cloud discovery and type device IDs, keys and IPs yourself.

discover.title: Select your pool devices
discover.description: Pick which of your discovered devices are the pool equipment. Local keys and IPs are filled in automatically. Leave a field empty if you don't have that device.

data.pump_switch: Sand filter pump — existing switch (any brand)

data_description.sensor: The AGP Smart Sensor / Water Analyzer (cloud-only device).
data_description.saltwater: The QS-series chlorinator — controlled locally over your LAN.
data_description.pump_tuya: Pick this only if your pump is itself a Tuya device.
data_description.pump_switch: Any existing Home Assistant switch (Shelly, Zigbee relay, …) that powers the pump.

manual.title: Manual setup
manual.description: Select the equipment you have. You can pick any combination.

sensor.title: Water sensor (cloud)
sensor.description: Enter your Tuya IoT developer-cloud credentials and the sensor's device id.

data_description.device_id: The analyzer's Tuya device id (Devices list on iot.tuya.com).

data_description.local_key: The device's local key — it rotates when the device is re-paired in the app.
data_description.host: The device's LAN IP (a DHCP reservation is recommended).
data_description.version: Tuya protocol version — leave on auto unless you know it.

data_description.pump_on_dp: The data point that switches the pump on/off (1 on most devices).

pump_entity.title: Existing pump entity
pump_entity.description: Link any pump (any brand) by selecting its switch and, optionally, its power/energy sensors.

data_description.pump_switch: The switch that powers the pump — enables Pump auto mode.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate Intex Pool
reauth_confirm.description: The credentials were rejected — usually because the Tuya local key rotated after the device was re-paired in the app. Enter the current value(s).

data_description.local_key: Current local key of the saltwater system.
data_description.pump_local_key: Current local key of the Tuya pump.
data_description.access_secret: Current Access Secret of your Tuya cloud project.

reconfigure_user.title: Reconfigure Intex Pool
reconfigure_user.description: Re-enter your Tuya cloud credentials to re-detect your devices — useful after replacing a device (it gets a new id).

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect — check the details and that the device is reachable.
error.invalid_auth: Credentials rejected — the local key or cloud secret is wrong (the local key changes when the device is re-paired).
error.need_creds: Enter your Tuya cloud Access ID and secret, or tick “set up manually”.
error.device_offline: That device wasn't found on your network — make sure it's powered on and on the same LAN as Home Assistant.
error.no_devices: No devices found for these credentials. Tick “set up manually instead” to enter them by hand, or double-check the region and Access ID/secret.

data_description.local_interval: How often the LAN devices (saltwater system, Tuya pump) are polled.
data_description.cloud_interval: How often the Tuya cloud (water sensor) is polled — keep modest, the free tier has a monthly call quota.
data_description.pool_volume: Enables the “Salt to add” advisor. Set to 0 to disable it.
data_description.salt_target: The salinity the advisor aims for (QS-series optimum is 950 ppm, range 800–1800).
data_description.pump_switch: The switch entity that drives your sand-filter pump.

no_schedule.message: No Intex Pool schedule available — this needs a loaded entry with a saltwater system and Tuya cloud credentials.

entry_not_found.message: No Intex Pool config entry with that id was found.

salt_alarm.title: Saltwater system alarm ({code})
salt_alarm.description: The saltwater system reports alarm {code}. Check the display and the manual's error-code table.

salt_alarm_e90.title: Saltwater system: low water flow (E90)
salt_alarm_e90.description: The saltwater system reports low or no pump flow (E90). Make sure the filter pump is running, valves are open and the flow sensor is clean (brush it gently with a plastic brush).

salt_alarm_e91e92.title: Saltwater system: salt out of range (E91/E92)
salt_alarm_e91e92.description: Salt is too low (E91) or too high (E92). For E91 add salt (≈0.15 g per litre raises ~100 ppm). For E92 drain and refill part of the pool per the manual's table.

salt_alarm_e01e02.title: Saltwater system: electrode fault (E01/E02)
salt_alarm_e01e02.description: Scale or dirt on the chlorine electrode, a loose electrode wire, or a failed electrode. Clean the electrode (vinegar soak); if it repeats, shorten the self-clean cycle or replace the electrode.

salt_alarm_e03e04.title: Saltwater system: water temperature out of range (E03/E04)
salt_alarm_e03e04.description: Water is below 10 °C (E03) or above 40 °C (E04). Stop using the system until the water temperature is back in range (run at night when too warm).

salt_alarm_e97.title: Saltwater system: internal fault (E97)
salt_alarm_e97.description: Internal PCB fault. The unit needs service — contact the service center.

salt_alarm_e99.title: Saltwater system: salt/temp sensor fault (E99)
salt_alarm_e99.description: The combined salt/temperature sensor is defective and needs replacing.

sensor_maintenance.title: Water sensor needs maintenance
sensor_maintenance.description: The water sensor reports that its probes need cleaning or calibration. Soak the sensor tips in white vinegar (up to 4 h), rinse, and calibrate pH/ORP in the app. Never let the probes dry out.

confirm.title: Force a fresh measurement
confirm.description: The newest measurement is from {last} — the sensor normally reports about once an hour. Confirming sends a refresh command that wakes the sensor for an immediate reading. Also check that the sensor is charged, in the water and online; if it never recovers, the device may have been re-paired with a new id (use Reconfigure).

set_schedule.name: Set saltwater schedule
set_schedule.description: Create, change or clear a saltwater-system schedule slot (written to the device via the Tuya cloud). Field meanings are best-effort.

slot.name: Slot
slot.description: Schedule slot to edit (0-6; 0 is the Boost cycle).

config_entry_id.name: Config entry
config_entry_id.description: Entry id of the Intex Pool integration to target. Only needed when more than one is set up.

clear.name: Clear
clear.description: Empty this slot instead of setting it.

enable.name: On
enable.description: Turn the system on for the schedule (off behaves like the boost cycle).

duration.name: Duration (hours)
duration.description: Run duration in hours (0-72, matching the schedule duration controls).

month.name: Month
month.description: Month for a one-time schedule (0 = unused).

date.name: Date
date.description: Day of month for a one-time schedule (0 = unused).

days.name: Days mask
days.description: Repeat bitmask (best-effort semantics): 255 = every day, 0 = one-time. Bit 7 marks a weekly repeat; bits 0-6 pick the weekday for one-time entries.

get_schedule.name: Get schedules
get_schedule.description: Returns the decoded schedule slots for the saltwater system and the water analyzer (measurement windows) as response data.

config_entry_id.name: Config entry
config_entry_id.description: Entry id of the Intex Pool integration to target. Only needed when more than one is set up.
